title: New York International Auto Show: a show site that reads like the show floor
tag: Auto show website, New York, NY. Launching December 2026
summaryLead: The New York International Auto Show has run since 1900. The new site puts the dates, the debuts and the rides up front, and cuts the news pile that buried them.
story: The New York International Auto Show is the oldest auto show in North America, ten days at the Javits Center every spring. The old site had the dates in the hero and then a long rail of news cards, tabs, an Instagram embed and tile grids, with stories from a show that had already closed still in the featured spot. Someone looking for when it opens, what's debuting and how to get there had to dig. The new site answers those first. Dates, venue, opening day and ticket status sit in one strip above the name. The name is set in Archivo and stretched to fill the width, the way a banner hangs over the floor. Everything else is asphalt, white and one signal red, kept for the ticket button.

numbers.label: H1 headings on the home page

goals: Put the dates, venue and ticket status on the first screen.
Show what's debuting and what you can ride.
Make getting to the Javits Center easy to plan.

features.title: The name, banner-sized
features.text: Four facts in a strip, then the show's name stretched to the full width. The floor photo below opens out as you scroll, with a count of days until the doors open.
features.alt: New York International Auto Show home page with the dates strip and the full-width name
features.story: Archivo is a variable font with a width axis, so the headline is sized and stretched in the browser to fit whatever screen it's on. Labels are Barlow.

features.title: Debuts on a departures board
features.text: Last year's debuts as a split-flap board: make, model and status. Hover a row and the car comes up below with its story.
features.alt: The 2026 debuts shown as a split-flap departures board
features.story: Every tile is a live character, not an image. Each one runs through a few random letters before it lands, so the board settles left to right like the real thing. With reduced motion on, it just shows the words.

features.title: The test track on a turntable
features.text: Scroll and the cars on the EV and hybrid test track come round one at a time, with the rider rules beside them.
features.alt: Cadillac Lyriq on the turntable in the EV and hybrid test track section
features.story: The section pins while you scroll and a ruler under the name tracks which car you're on. The platform is drawn in SVG and CSS, so the only images are the cars.

features.text: Camp Jeep, the EV track, exotics, tuner cars and the rest, each with one line on what it is.

impactNote: Projected from published research. We'll replace these with the show's own numbers after launch.

impact.text: of viewing time goes to the first screen and 74% to the first two. The old ticket link sat 2.1 screens down on desktop and 2.7 on a phone. Ticket alerts now sit in the header, and ticket status is in the first strip.
impact.source: Nielsen Norman Group, Scrolling and Attention

impact.text: more retail conversions for every 0.1 seconds a mobile site got faster, across 37 brands. The new home page paints its largest element half a second sooner and downloads 89% less.
impact.source: Google and Deloitte, Milliseconds Make Millions

impact.text: the e-commerce conversion rate for pages that load in 1 second compared with pages that load in 5. On a 25 Mbps connection, the old home page's images alone took about two minutes to finish.
impact.source: Portent, Site Speed and Conversion Rate

impact.text: structured data lets Google show the show's dates and venue in search results. The old home page had none, and its 40 H1 headings left search engines guessing what the page was about.
impact.source: Google Search Central, Event structured data

statement: The New York International Auto Show is the oldest in North America: ten days at the Javits Center every spring since 1900. The old site opened on a video, then buried the dates, the debuts and the ticket link under news from a show that had already closed. We rebuilt the home page around what people come for: when it's on, what's new and how to get there.
brief: We started from the questions people ask before they buy a ticket: when, what's new, what can I ride and how do I get there. Every section on the new home page answers one of them.
closing: Dates, debuts and directions first. Everything else is one click away.
